source.title: JEDI: JEPA-to-Edge Distillation for Efficient Cropland Segmentation from Satellite Imagery
source.authors: Kishor Kumar Bhaumik; Nicolas Roque dos Santos; Jia Chen; Evangelos E. Papalexakis

record.file_problem: The text is complete and readable, with minor formatting and character-encoding artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses teacher–student representation alignment as part of a distillation method for cropland segmentation. Its reported outcomes measure segmentation performance, not whether representations converge, become interchangeable, or share features.
record.gate_note: The paper applies a learned cross-architecture projection and feature-alignment loss, and ablates alignment components. It does not report a representation-similarity or alignment-loss outcome. The reported segmentation results therefore do not measure any claim version; the alignment-related ablation outcomes are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study uses a learned affine projection to align a SegFormer student to a frozen I-JEPA teacher for distillation. It reports only segmentation mIoU/F1 and efficiency, never a representation-similarity, alignment-loss or mapping-loss value. Its own method's performance does not bear on whether representations converge or are interchangeable.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that pre-task representation alignment plus persistent alignment during adaptation improve CalCROP21 segmentation, most under aggressive compression (B0 +16 mIoU), and give a favorable accuracy–compute trade-off. They make no convergence claim. One correction: their text says persistent alignment causes the largest degradation when removed, but Table III shows removing Stage 1 costs more (63.0 vs 65.0).
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an MSE feature-reconstruction objective through a learned affine projection, plus segmentation and response-distillation losses. It does not use or evaluate the original sources’ convergence measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: For MiT-B0, removing Stage 1 alignment (63.0) or persistent feature alignment (65.0) lowers mIoU relative to full JEDI (68.0). The standalone student scores 52.0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-level alignment to a large ViT teacher through an affine projection improves a compact student's downstream segmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher choice strongly changes student mIoU under identical alignment: I-JEPA 68.0, supervised ViT 54.5, DINO 36.0 (Table IV).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The usefulness of aligning a student to a teacher's representation depends on the teacher's pretraining objective.

record.problems: The study evaluates one dataset and region and a binary segmentation task. The alignment ablations report downstream segmentation scores rather than direct measurements of representation similarity or interchangeability.
record.rows_left_out: Other Table II segmentation results compare distillation methods and student capacities but do not measure a claim-version outcome. The response-distillation ablation (Table III) is not an alignment result.

untested.parts: No alignment measured across model scale; the B0/B1/B2 comparison is of mIoU, not representation similarity.
No vision-language or paired image-caption representations.
Five seeds are used only for mIoU spread; no cross-seed representation comparison.
The affine projection is trained but its reconstruction loss or mapping quality is never reported; no stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping.
No interpretable features or circuits compared.
No alternative similarity metrics or input distributions.
No test of plateau, completeness, or data/objective causes of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 / uses_without_test classification is correct. The teacher-choice result (Table IV) is not recorded as a row, but it is method performance and does not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison measures representation alignment across model scale or capability.
No paired image-caption or vision-language representation comparison.
Five-seed performance summaries are reported, but representations or shared subspaces across seeds are not measured.

The paper trains a projection to align teacher and student features, but does not report whether the representations are mapped with little loss or evaluate stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified or compared.
No alternative representation-similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions are compared.
The study does not test whether shared data or objectives explain representation alignment, nor whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete.
